chunks: My father, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say:

Fear God, and you must fulfill trusts to those who have entrusted you. For even if the killer of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) were to entrust me with something, I would certainly fulfill that trust to him.

key_terms.اتقوا: Fear God, be God-conscious (taqwa); an imperative commanding piety and mindfulness of divine accountability
key_terms.الأمانة: Trust, something entrusted; a fundamental moral and legal obligation in Islam encompassing property, secrets, and responsibilities
key_terms.قاتل أمير المؤمنين: The killer of the Commander of the Faithful; refers to Ibn Muljam who assassinated Imam Ali (AS)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about fulfilling trusts even to enemies?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the absolute obligation of fulfilling trusts (amanah) in this teaching delivered to his companions. The Imam makes a striking statement to illustrate the unconditional nature of trustworthiness: even the murderer of Imam Ali (AS) -- the most heinous criminal in the Imam's eyes -- would have his trust honored. This underscores that trustworthiness is a universal moral obligation not contingent upon one's relationship with or feelings toward the entrustor.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to me. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrate to us from Ibrahim b. Hashim from Isma`il b. Marar from Yunus b. `Abd al-Rahman from `Umar b. Yazid. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) say:
Fear Allah and betake to fulfilling trusts to those who have entrusted you. Even if the killer of Amir al-Mu’minin (as) were to entrust something to me, I would fulfill the trust to him.
